Oct 29-Oct 30: 9:00 am – 3:00 pmOffices and Issues To Appear On Ballot and Lists of Candidates 
Under an assigned alternating sequence required by state law, candidates of the Democratic Party will be listed first on the Johnson County ballot this year and in 2028. Republicans were listed first in 2022 and 2024. 
All offices will include a write-in line even if no candidates filed.

The filing deadline for most offices has passed. Exceptions:
Candidates for the Agricultural Extension Council and the Soil and Water Commission may file with our office until 5 p.m. on August 26.
The two full status parties (Democratic and Republican) may nominate candidates by convention until 5 p.m. on August 26. The filing deadline for candidates for partisan office not representing the two full status parties was June 2 at 5 p.m.
Ballot issues may be added.
A statewide list of federal and state candidates is available at the Secretary of State's website.
Sample ballots will be available on our Polling Place Lookup in September. You can use the polling place lookup to find your districts, and then review the list of candidates.Federal Offices

Public Measure 1: Iowa Constitutional Amendment - Taxation Limitations (50% required)
Summary: Provides that any bill that increases the individual income tax rate or the corporate income tax rate, or the rate of any other type of tax based upon income or legal and special reserves, shall require the affirmative votes of at least two-thirds of the members elected to each house of the general assembly for passage. Further, the two-thirds majority vote requirement applies to the passage of a bill that establishes a new tax on any type of income or legal and special reserves imposed by the state. The requirement excludes to taxes imposed at the option of a local government. A lawsuit challenging the proper enactment of a bill under this section must be filed no later than one year following the enactment.
The Constitution of the State of Iowa is amended by adding the following new section to new Article XIII:
ARTICLE XIII. TAXATION LIMITATIONS. Section 1. Two-thirds majority vote for state tax law changes.
Passage of a bill that increases the individual income tax rate or the corporate income tax rate, or the rate of any other type of tax based upon income or legal and special reserves, shall require the affirmative votes of at least two-thirds of the members elected to each house of the general assembly. This requirement does not apply to taxes imposed at the option of a local government. Passage of a bill that establishes a new tax on any type of income or legal and special reserves imposed by the state shall require the affirmative votes of at least two-thirds of the members elected to each house of the general assembly. A lawsuit challenging the proper enactment of a bill under this section must be filed no later than one year following the enactment. If such a lawsuit is not filed within the one-year limit, the bill shall be considered properly enacted under this section. Each bill to which this section applies must include a separate provision describing the requirements for enactment prescribed by this section. The general assembly shall enact laws to implement this section.

Public Measure LY: County Jail Bond (60% required)

Shall the County of Johnson, State of Iowa, issue its general obligation bonds in an amount not exceeding the amount of $94,500,000 for the purpose of acquiring land and constructing, equipping and furnishing a new sheriff’s office and jail facility?

Public Measure LZ: City of Hills Bond (60% required)
Shall the City of Hills, in Johnson County, State of Iowa, enter into a loan agreement and issue general obligation bonds in an amount not exceeding $5,100,000 for the purpose of paying the cost, to that extent, of constructing furnishing and equipping a municipal building, including fire protection and city hall functionalities?

Public Measure MA: Lone Tree Community School District Bond (60% required)

Shall the Board of Directors of the Lone Tree Community School District in the Counties of Johnson and Louisa, State of Iowa, be authorized to contract indebtedness and issue General Obligation Bonds in an amount not to exceed $6,900,000 to provide funds to remodel, repair, and improve the school building for energy efficiency, including HVAC, mechanical, electrical, and site improvements? 
 
Public Measure VF: Mid-Prairie Community School District Bond (60% required)
Shall the Board of Directors of the Mid-Prairie Community School District in the Counties of Washington, Iowa, and Johnson, State of Iowa, be authorized to contract indebtedness and issue General Obligation Bonds in an amount not to exceed $19,000,000 to provide funds to build, furnish, and equip an addition to the high school, including a new events entrance, auditorium, and fine arts classrooms, with related remodeling and improvements and related site improvements; and to renovate, improve, furnish and equip several existing special education and general education classrooms? 

Public Measure NC: Kirkwood Community College bond (60% required)
Shall Kirkwood Community College (Merged Area X) in the Counties of Benton, Black Hawk, Buchanan, Cedar, Clinton, Delaware, Dubuque, Iowa, Jackson, Jefferson, Johnson, Jones, Keokuk, Linn, Louisa, Poweshiek, Tama, and Washington, be authorized to renovate, improve, erect, and equip facilities to modernize learning spaces with an emphasis on health sciences, industrial technologies, agricultural sciences, and business and information technology, contract indebtedness therefor, and issue General Obligation Bonds in an amount not exceeding $88,000,000 for those purposes?
